provenance.covers: the factory set cards and which parallels cover every base card
provenance.notes: Confirms 66 of the 67 checklists it lists once the two series are summed; the exception is Legendary Homefield Advantage, counted 5 per series where the Topps PDFs print LHA-1 to LHA-5 and LHA-6 to LHA-9, so the manufacturer stands. Sole source for the two Factory Set checklists here, which are in neither series PDF. It states "All 700 base cards are available in the following parallels" and lists 42, recorded here as coverage: full. It qualifies Black as Series Two only, which the repo owner corrected: Black prints all 700. Names are taken from base.csv rather than from this source, which prints "Colby Mayo" for Topps' Coby Mayo at #20. Its KRC designation on the short-print rookies is not adopted: Topps prints "Rookie", and the kayfabe idea it marks is a category, recorded as a tag. It lists Printing Plates as one entry, "set of four for each card". They are declared as four — Black, Cyan, Magenta, Yellow — because a plate is a distinct one-of-one card a collector owns, and one entry cannot record owning the cyan plate of a given card. The count is this source's; the four colour names are the standard printing set, and TCDB names 2026's plates exactly so. Its Big Apple checklist prints #658 Gleyber Torres where the Topps Series 2 PDF prints #656 Jairo Iriarte in that section; the manufacturer's card stands. The 99 they agree on match exactly. Serial numbering is recorded only where a source states it outright for a given parallel: 2025 has 164 of 330 numbered and 2026 has 41 of 440, all from that source's parallel lists as transcribed by the repo owner. The rest carry no print_run and that is deliberate. Its relic and autograph ratio tables give card counts without print runs, so those 133 parallels stay unnumbered rather than take the /150-/99-/50-/25-/10-/5 ladder their neighbours use, which would be inference. An estimate for an unnumbered card is not a print run either: the 1990 inserts' Pink is described as limited to 600 copies but not serial-numbered, so it gets none. Serial numbers were then cross-checked against Trading Card Database's 2025 Topps Inserts and Related Sets listing: 44 agreed exactly and none conflicted, and 70 more were filled from it. That listing also supplies 24 parallels this source omits for lists it does carry — the eleven the 1990 All-Stars insert prints beyond Blue Nameplate, the OPS Bests ladder, Summer Superstars Red, Dynamic Duos Black, 2024 First Pitch Autographs FoilFractor, and Rounding the Bases Dual Relics Platinum and Red. Nothing was added for a list this source does not carry: Carrying the Flag and Mesmerized turned out to belong to 2025 Topps Flagship Collection and Hidden Gems to 2025 Topps Chrome Hidden Gems, both separate products. The two disagree on one figure, the Mega Box Black foil of the 1990 insert: this source calls it a one-of-one and TCDB numbers it to 10, where every other programme in the set puts Black at 10 and reserves the one-of-one for a FoilFractor. The repo owner settled it at 10, so TCDB's figure stands. That source also names these Crackle Foilboard and omits the Purple /75 this repo holds.

provenance.covers: True Photo and Team Color Border as full base parallels; the 582 Montgomery Club factory set parallel
provenance.notes: Both print all 700 base cards in 2025 and are declared coverage: full on that assertion alone. Baseball Card Pedia omits them from its list of parallels covering the whole base set, while listing Vintage Stock and Clear, which print all 700 the same year. Its 2026 page says of all four "after years as full parallels, the following are now 200-card partial-parallels", so the omission is that list being incomplete rather than these two being partial in 2025. The 582 Montgomery Club factory set, sold to club members, prints every base card with a sublimated 582 Club logo, so it is declared coverage: full. The box itself is not declared as a packaging: a packaging lists checklist files it contains and this one holds a parallel, which has no file, so the schema cannot yet say what is in it.

notes: One set issued in two waves. In The Name Relics stays per series: the two checklists reuse codes on different players, so one file would break card_number uniqueness. Four sections Topps labels a variation or short print number their own cards and share no number with any checklist, so they are declared as the autograph and insert lists they are, not as variations.
